name: Bräus Gotland
description: Bräus is an unusual partnership trick-taking game from the Swedish island of Gotland, played by two teams of two or three using a 36-card pack stripped from the standard deck.

content.text: Bräus is an unusual partnership trick-taking game from the Swedish island of Gotland, played by two teams of two or three using a 36-card pack stripped from the standard deck.

Country/Region of Origin: Sweden (Gotland)
Time Period: Medieval roots via the Karnöffel family; modern Gotland rules documented in the late 20th century.
Historical Development: Local descendant of the German Karnöffel group, adapted and preserved as a regional partnership game on Gotland.
Cultural Significance: Traditional island game still played socially in Gotland, showcasing an unusual hierarchy of special cards and sevens-as-tricks.

Minimum Players: 4
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: Two teams of two or three players.

Type: Standard 36-card deck (2–5 removed from each suit)
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included

Standard 36-card deck
Score sheet (optional)
Table space
Four-player game: 9 cards per player. Six-player game: 6 cards per player. Dealing Pattern: Clockwise, with the player to dealer's right cutting.

items.text: Four-player Bräus (two teams of two): Canonical Bräus table with four players in two partnerships; each player is dealt nine cards from the 36-card pack.
Six-player Bräus (two teams of three): Extended Bräus table with six players in two partnerships of three; each player is dealt six cards from the 36-card pack.
